answer.rationale:
Constraints prune the option set before memory does. rollback_release is ruled out by compliance regardless of how well memory_b1 worked. enable_circuit_breaker (memory_b4) fails fast by design, which directly conflicts with 'without losing customer writes' at settlement peak. regional_failover (memory_b2) recovered a latency degradation, but that record is about latency during an unspecified load profile; shifting regions mid-peak with heavy in-flight writes risks exactly the write loss the objective forbids. add_capacity (memory_b3) succeeded because headroom was provisioned BEFORE the peak; we are 90 minutes into the event, so the mechanism that made it work is unavailable. That leaves route_read_replicas: memory_b5's mechanism (take non-transactional read load off the primary so write latency recovers) is the closest match to the observed symptom, a write-path p99 climb under read+write contention, and it is additive and reversible rather than traffic-shedding.

Verification targets are the two records my reasoning actually leans on. memory_b5 is load-bearing for the chosen action and I need the original to check whether the write-latency recovery was attributable to replica routing or merely coincident with load subsiding, and whether the primary was contended the same way. memory_b3 is the strongest alternative and I need to confirm the pre-provisioning timing, because if capacity can be added hot within the window it may beat replica routing. I deliberately did not spend budget on memory_b1 (moot) or memory_b4/memory_b2 (excluded on objective grounds, not on evidence quality) — verifying them could not change the decision.

Staged as a small guarded test: route a bounded slice of report/dashboard queries first with a fast revert path, confirm primary write p99 responds, then widen. A broad rollout during peak would be an untested bet on a single archived record.

Downstream value risk: replica reads are stale by replication lag, and this is a payments platform. If settlement reconciliation, balance checks, or risk/limit decisions read from these replicas, stale reads could silently produce wrong money-affecting outcomes that look like success on the latency dashboard. Routing must be restricted to genuinely non-authoritative reporting queries, with anything on the settlement decision path pinned to the primary. Also note replica lag may itself worsen if the primary is already saturated.

Uncertainty retained: the true cause of the 90-minute climb is not established. The new release is 2 hours old and correlates in time, so it remains a plausible driver even though reverting is off the table; if it is the cause, replica routing buys headroom without fixing anything and a targeted forward fix or feature-level mitigation is the real remedy in the next window. Every inherited record here is a success story with no recorded failures, which is a survivorship-biased sample and a reason to hold these priors loosely. I am treating this as symptom relief plus diagnosis, not a resolution.
